rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

⚡ DONE — Complete Speak Plurals, then return to your day.

2. At Predict Different, ask, “What would count as evidence against my first answer?”.
3. When you reach Speak Plurals, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: One explanation is a guess wearing a crown.

rituals.title: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.name: ADD THE PREFIX
rituals.unique_game_move: Begin where it says Prefix Thought; stop the moment you complete Resume Task.
rituals.recognition_cue: Add The Prefix gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.situation: Add The Prefix gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.immediate_need: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.challenge: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Add The Prefix gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Prefix Thought; stop the moment you complete Resume Task.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ADD THE PREFIX // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Resume Task be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Prefix Thought, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Check Command, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Resume Task, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

rituals.potency_2: At Check Command, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
rituals.potency_3: When you reach Resume Task, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.
rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can finish at Resume Task even if the original thought has not completely disappeared.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”
rituals.formula_flow: Prefix Thought → Check Command → Resume Task

rituals.title: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.name: THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.
rituals.unique_game_move: Play from Ask Danger to Respect. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.recognition_cue: Try Thanks, Mind. No Contract. when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.situation: Try Thanks, Mind. No Contract. when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.immediate_need: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.challenge: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Try Thanks, Mind. No Contract. when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.

GAME MOVE
Play from Ask Danger to Respect. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT. // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Respect and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Ask Danger, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Answer M, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Respect, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By the time you reach Respect, the problem looks a little more workable.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just chose one move that matched what matters to me.”
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not dismiss warnings that point to concrete and immediate danger.

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.plain:
THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT.

TRIGGER
Values, meaning & loss

PLAY TIME
about 1 minute

HOOK
Try Thanks, Mind. No Contract. when the immediate feeling has pulled you away from what matters. It creates just enough space for a different response.

GOAL
Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.

GAME MOVE
Play from Ask Danger to Respect. Treat the last move as the finish line.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THANKS, MIND. NO CONTRACT. // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Ask Danger — Ask what danger the thought is trying to prevent.
2. Thank Intention — Offer a precise thank-you for that intention.
3. Answer M — Then answer: ‘I’m not signing this instruction.’ Choose a matching what matters to you action that keeps any useful caution but rejects the controlling move.
4. Respect — Respect the alarm; decline the contract.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Respect and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Ask Danger, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Answer M, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Respect, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Protection can be acknowledged without being hired.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By the time you reach Respect, the problem looks a little more workable.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just chose one move that matched what matters to me.”

FORMULA FLOW
Ask Danger → Thank Intention → Answer M → Respect

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Rigid beliefs, labels & stories

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
When an old rule is being treated like a fact, Thought Departures gives you something concrete to do with the moment.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Give thought transport, not a throne.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Place Thought to Allow Departure.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THOUGHT DEPARTURES // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Departure closes the round.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Place Thought, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Return Eyes, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Allow Departure, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give thought transport, not a throne.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can reach Allow Departure with more choice than you had at Place Thought.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found a rule I had never actually chosen.”

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 NAME THE SERIES // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Ignore — Ignore today’s plot for ten seconds.
2. Ask Recurring — Ask what recurring series it belongs to: ‘The Rejection Forecast,’ ‘Everyone Is Ahead,’ ‘I Must Fix It Now.’ Give the series a short title and season number.
3. Ask Whether — Then ask whether this episode contains new information or recycled footage.

⚡ END MOVE — Ask Whether. No second lap.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PASSENGER THOUGHT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Choose Time — Choose one two-minute action that matters.
2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Keep hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
4. Actually — At the destination, Notice who actually drove.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Actually and release the exercise.

1. To open Choose Time, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Keep Hands, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Actually, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.

🎮 CAMERA FIRST, CAPTION SECOND // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Fifteen — For fifteen seconds, collect camera data: colour, movement, sound, pressure, position.
2. Describe Event — Then say the event using only that footage.
3. Add Meaning — On a new line, add the meaning and Notice it CAPTION.
4. Keep Never — Keep both; never confuse their sources.

⚡ END MOVE — Keep Never. No second lap.

rituals.unique_game_move: Use Choose Ordinary as the doorway and Participation as the exit.
rituals.recognition_cue: Enter The Action works best when good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
rituals.situation: Enter The Action works best when good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
rituals.immediate_need: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.challenge: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Perfectionism & performance pressure

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Enter The Action works best when good enough is being rejected unless it is flawless. The goal is not to win an argument with your mind—just change the next move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.

GAME MOVE
Use Choose Ordinary as the doorway and Participation as the exit.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ENTER THE ACTION // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Participation is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Choose Ordinary, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Leave Re, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Participation, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found the point where enough really was enough.”

rituals.title: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.name: THE ATTENTION BOUNCER
rituals.unique_game_move: One round only: enter at Spot Arrival, finish at Return Door.
rituals.recognition_cue: Try The Attention Bouncer when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.situation: Try The Attention Bouncer when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.immediate_need: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.challenge: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Try The Attention Bouncer when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing. It creates just enough space for a different response.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Spot Arrival, finish at Return Door.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE ATTENTION BOUNCER // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Spot Arrival — Notice the next thought without following it.
2. Stamp Access — Stamp it REQUESTED, RELEVANT, or UNINVITED.
3. Set Budget — Give only the chosen category a short timer; let the others wait without argument.
4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Return Door and release the exercise.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Spot Arrival, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Set Budget, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Return Door, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.

rituals.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By the time you reach Return Door, the problem looks a little more workable.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just moved attention from what was loud to what was useful.”
rituals.formula_flow: Spot Arrival → Stamp Access → Set Budget → Return Door

Not every thought gets the same access to your attention.

One round only: enter at Spot Arrival, finish at Return Door.

🎮 THE ATTENTION BOUNCER // PLAY

4. Return Door — When the timer ends, return to the task or deliberately admit one new thought.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Return Door and release the exercise.

1. To open Spot Arrival, slow the next movement by about half.

By the time you reach Return Door, the problem looks a little more workable.

“I just moved attention from what was loud to what was useful.”

rituals.immediate_need: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.challenge: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
One Clean Wish is a tiny mind game for the moment when your responsibility and someone else's have blurred together.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.

GAME MOVE
Touch Bring Person, follow the moves, and finish on Dont Cancel.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ONE CLEAN WISH // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance.
2. Dont Deny — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.
3. State Boundary — Then state the boundary or action you still need.
4. Dont Cancel — Warmth does not cancel discernment.

⚡ DONE — Complete Dont Cancel, then return to your day.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Bring Person, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At State Boundary, separate responsibility from punishment.
3. When you reach Dont Cancel, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found where my responsibility ends.”

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE 2% SOFTENING // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while looking at one neutral object.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.

⚡ FINISH — Ask Whether closes the round.

1. Before you begin Release Forehead, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Hold Neutral, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Ask Whether, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.

⚡ END MOVE — Claim Control. No second lap.

🎮 ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present.
4. Adjust — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Adjust, you are done.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Choose Stable, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Anchor Verify, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Adjust, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The first interpretation feels less final when you reach Adjust.

📸 MY RESULT
“The alarm came from then; I found evidence of now.”

Choose Stable → Keep Most → Anchor Verify → Adjust

🎮 NO FAVOURITE SENSATION // PLAY

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL

Start at Find Five and keep going only until Answer Blue.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE SENSE ROLL CALL // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Find Five — Find five distinct colours or shapes, four contact sensations, three separate sounds, two scents, and one taste or mouth sensation.
2. Answer Blue — No generic answers; ‘blue attention’ beats ‘something blue.’ Let the inventory end with the most stable item.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Answer Blue is your cue to stop.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Carry Final, you are done.

1–2 minutes

HOOK

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Walking can become a moving attention track.

GAME MOVE
Play from Place Weight to Finish Walking. Treat the last move as the finish line.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Finish Walking and release the exercise.

1. To open Place Weight, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Thought, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Finish Walking, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Walking can become a moving attention track.

GAME MOVE
Play from Place Weight to Finish Walking. Treat the last move as the finish line.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Finish Walking and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Place Weight, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Thought, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Finish Walking, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Walking can become a moving attention track.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By the time you reach Finish Walking, the problem looks a little more workable.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just moved attention from what was loud to what was useful.”

Place Weight → Follow Events → Thought → Finish Walking

rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Turn attention toward the fact that experience is known.

GAME MOVE
Enter through Choose Sensation; leave as soon as you reach Return Fact. One pass is enough.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 NOTICE THE NOTICING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact.

⚡ DONE — Complete Return Fact, then return to your day.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE BREATH HINGE // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Follow Inhale — Follow a natural inhale to the instant it turns toward exhale.
2. Dont Hold — Do not hold or stretch the hinge.
3. Change — Notice the same effortless change at the bottom of exhalation.
4. Allow Breaths — Visit each threshold lightly, then allow several breaths to pass unwatched.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Breaths closes the round.

3. When you reach Allow Breaths, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Rest where one phase becomes another.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 WHERE SOUND BECOMES HEARING // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Listen Sustained — Listen to a sustained, gentle sound.
2. Follow Apparent — Follow it from apparent distance toward the place where it becomes an auditory experience—ear, head, body, or nowhere locatable.
3. Rest Briefly — When the border between outside vibration and inside hearing blurs, rest there briefly.

⚡ END MOVE — Rest Briefly. No second lap.

rituals.name: BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH
rituals.unique_game_move: Use Open Sky as the doorway and Allow Attention as the exit.
rituals.recognition_cue: Borrow The Sky’S Width is for the moment when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.situation: Borrow The Sky’S Width is for the moment when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.immediate_need: Let vision teach attention another size.
rituals.challenge: Let vision teach attention another size.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Attention & cognitive overload

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Borrow The Sky’S Width is for the moment when your mind is stuck on the loudest thing—before the reaction gets to choose for you.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Let vision teach attention another size.

GAME MOVE
Use Open Sky as the doorway and Allow Attention as the exit.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Open Sky — Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release Pinpoint — Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Compare Width — Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
4. Allow Attention — Allow attention to occupy both.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Allow Attention is your cue to stop.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you enter Open Sky, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
2. At Compare Width, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Allow Attention, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The round ends on this idea: Let vision teach attention another size.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Keep Image be enough.

rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
If the old reaction is running before you notice it, Catch Wanting Before The Object turns the mental noise into one playable move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Wait Pull, finish at Name Object.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Name Object and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Wait Pull, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Observe Wanting, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Name Object, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

GOAL
Release both hands of mental grasping.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Whether first, Act According last.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Whether — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Act According, you are done.

rituals.hook: Not For, Not Against is a tiny mind game for the moment when one rejection is starting to feel bigger than the whole picture.
rituals.mission: Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.game_move: Give yourself one clean run: Whether first, Act According last.
rituals.how_to_play:
🎮 NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Whether — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Act According, you are done.
rituals.power_up_1: When you arrive at Whether, press both feet down for three seconds.
rituals.power_up_2: At Let Content, separate responsibility from punishment.
rituals.power_up_3: When you reach Act According, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Release both hands of mental grasping.
rituals.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By Act According, the first reaction is no longer the only move on the table.

📸 MY RESULT
“A rejection hurt; it didn't get to define my value.”

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REMOVE THE NAME BADGES // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Name — Name the roles active today.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Release Roles be enough.

rituals.plain:
REMOVE THE NAME BADGES

TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Remove The Name Badges catches the moment when the old reaction is running before you notice it and gives you another route.

GOAL
See what remains when roles clock out briefly.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Name; stop the moment you complete Release Roles.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REMOVE THE NAME BADGES // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Name — Name the roles active today.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Release Roles be enough.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. As you begin Name, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Imagine Badge, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Release Roles, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: See what remains when roles clock out briefly.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You reach Release Roles with a clearer distinction between the reaction and the response.

📸 MY RESULT
“I caught the pattern early enough to choose.”

FORMULA FLOW
Name → Imagine Badge → Release Roles

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Read Order and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Name Mix, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Link Cue, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Read Order, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: Feelings that seem tangled may be answering different moments.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE THREE QUALITIES WEATHER REPORT // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Classify — Classify the current movement as clarity, agitation, inertia, or a mixture.
2. Speed — Notice its speed, energy, and attentional style.
3. Choose Smallest — Choose the smallest balancing condition—rest for agitation, body alarm for inertia, protection for clarity.
4. Say Recheck — Recheck later without saying ‘I am this.’.

⚡ END MOVE — Say Recheck. No second lap.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Classify, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Choose Smallest, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Say Recheck, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Mental states are climates, not surnames.

rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Count Gap be enough.

rituals.plain_text:
DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Do Not Replace The Last Thought gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

GOAL
Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Wait Thought; stop the moment you complete Count Gap.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Count Gap be enough.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Wait Thought, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Rest Duration, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Count Gap, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can finish at Count Gap even if the original thought has not completely disappeared.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

🎮 DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE // PLAY

rituals.challenge: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.
rituals.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
Third-Person Ownership Test gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.
rituals.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Describe Event; stop the moment you complete Distance.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Describe Event — Say the event once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Distance be enough.
rituals.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Describe Event, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Return Person, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Distance, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CALL THE INNER COUNCIL // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Give Self — Give each self-state a seat.
2. Sentence — One sentence each: what I need, what I fear, what I propose.

Run the sequence once. Introduce opens it; Keep Words closes it.
rituals.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Keep Words, you are done.

2. At Name Wrong, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Keep Words, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Remember the point: The remembered self deserves credible rethought.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE WORLDS, ONE FACT // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Keep Event — Keep the event fixed.
2. Invent — Invent three models for why it happened.
3. Predict Different — Each model must predict a different thing you could observe next.
4. Earliest — Notice the earliest observation that would separate them.
5. Speak Plurals — Until that evidence arrives, speak in plurals: possibilities, not prophecy.

⚡ DONE — Complete Speak Plurals, then return to your day.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

Begin where it says Prefix Thought; stop the moment you complete Resume Task.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ADD THE PREFIX // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Prefix Thought — Take the exact thought and place these words before it: ‘I am noticing my mind produce…’ Say the complete sentence once at ordinary speed.
2. Check Command — Notice what remains true and what loses command authority.
3. Resume Task — Carry on with the next chosen task while the sentence exists nearby.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Resume Task be enough.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Prefix Thought, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Check Command, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Resume Task, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can turn a fact back into an event.

GOAL
Give thought transport, not a throne.

GAME MOVE
Move through the sequence once, from Place Thought to Allow Departure.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THOUGHT DEPARTURES // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Departure closes the round.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Place Thought, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Return Eyes, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
3. When you reach Allow Departure, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give thought transport, not a throne.

items.how_to_play:
🎮 THOUGHT DEPARTURES // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Place Thought — Place the thought on something already moving: a bus passing, a leaf in drainage water, subtitles leaving a screen.
2. Watch Arrival — Watch its full arrival and departure without pushing it faster.
3. Return Eyes — When the carrier exits, return your eyes to one stationary object.
4. Allow Departure — Another vehicle may come; none owns the station.

⚡ FINISH — Allow Departure closes the round.

items.power_up_2: At Return Eyes, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
items.power_up_3: When you reach Allow Departure, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Give thought transport, not a throne.

Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
If your mind keeps delaying the first move, Passenger Thought turns the mental noise into one playable move.

GOAL
You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Choose Time, finish at Actually.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PASSENGER THOUGHT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Choose Time — Choose one two-minute action that matters.
2. Ride Passenger — Invite the thought to ride in the passenger seat—audible, uncomfortable, unedited.
3. Keep Hands — Keep hands on the action wheel and complete the movement while it talks.
4. Actually — At the destination, Notice who actually drove.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Actually and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Choose Time, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Keep Hands, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Actually, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: You do not need an empty vehicle to steer.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The pattern becomes easier to spot before you commit to Actually.

📸 MY RESULT
“I just stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

FORMULA FLOW
Choose Time → Ride Passenger → Keep Hands → Actually

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 MAKE A WIDER CONTAINER // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Locate Unwanted — Locate the unwanted sensation.
2. Find Edges — Find its edges.
3. Soften Muscles — Soften the muscles around—not inside—it.

⚡ EXIT — Finish Enlarging and leave the game there.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.

GAME MOVE
Use Choose Ordinary as the doorway and Participation as the exit.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ENTER THE ACTION // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Participation is your cue to stop.

items.how_to_play:
🎮 ENTER THE ACTION // PLAY
Stay with the sequence. You do not need to improve it.

1. Choose Ordinary — Choose one ordinary activity.
2. Place Vision — Place vision, touch, posture, and hearing inside it.
3. Leave Re — When attention leaves, re-enter through the next physical contact point rather than scolding yourself.
4. Stay Activity — Stay until the activity reaches its natural edge.
5. Participation — Participation, not perfect focus, is the target.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Participation is your cue to stop.
items.power_up_1: As you enter Choose Ordinary, feel where your body is supported for one moment.
items.power_up_2: At Leave Re, try the opposite possibility for ten seconds.
items.power_up_3: When you reach Participation, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Leave the exercise with this: Stop watching yourself do the thing; do the thing.
items.win_reward_raw:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can do Participation while some discomfort is still present.

📸 MY RESULT
“I found the point where enough really was enough.”
items.formula_flow_raw: Choose Ordinary → Place Vision → Leave Re → Stay Activity → Participation

items.recognition_cue: One Clean Wish is a tiny mind game for the moment when your responsibility and someone else's have blurred together.
items.situation: One Clean Wish is a tiny mind game for the moment when your responsibility and someone else's have blurred together.
items.immediate_need: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.challenge: Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.
items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Boundaries & over-responsibility

PLAY TIME
1–2 minutes

HOOK
One Clean Wish is a tiny mind game for the moment when your responsibility and someone else's have blurred together.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Goodwill can interrupt hostility without pretending closeness.

GAME MOVE
Touch Bring Person, follow the moves, and finish on Dont Cancel.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ONE CLEAN WISH // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Bring Person — Bring the person to mind at a safe distance.
2. Dont Deny — Choose one honest wish that does not deny harm: ‘May we both be free from causing more suffering,’ or ‘May safety become possible.’ Offer it once.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.

GAME MOVE
Start at Release Forehead. Stop at Ask Whether. Let the middle do the work.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE 2% SOFTENING // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Release Forehead — Without forcing happiness, release the forehead, loosen the eyes, and lift the mouth corners by only two percent.
2. Keep Expression — Keep the expression believable.
3. Hold Neutral — Hold it while looking at one neutral object.
4. Ask Whether — Ask whether defence changed by even half a notch.

⚡ FINISH — Ask Whether closes the round.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Release Forehead, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Hold Neutral, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Ask Whether, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: Your face can send the nervous system a quieter memo.

items.goal_why_game_move:

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PLAY THE BODY PASSWORD // PLAY
Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.

⚡ END MOVE — Claim Control. No second lap.

Do the moves once and let the result be whatever it is.

1. Set Code — Choose three tiny comfortable movements, such as tap a knee, touch a thumb, and look at one fixed object. Say the order once.
2. Run Order — Perform A–B–C slowly, pausing after each movement long enough to feel it finish.
3. Reverse Code — Perform C–B–A at the same pace. If you lose the order, return to neutral and restart instead of speeding up.
4. Claim Control — Name the movement you directed most clearly, then let the whole code stop.

⚡ END MOVE — Claim Control. No second lap.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Just before you start Set Code, notice one sound in the room before continuing.
2. At Reverse Code, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Claim Control, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Take this line with you: A short body code can prove that alarm has not taken every control.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
At Claim Control, you have at least one option the first reaction did not show you.

📸 MY RESULT
“My body sounded an alarm; I didn't have to turn it into danger.”

FORMULA FLOW
Set Code → Run Order → Reverse Code → Claim Control

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE FOUR-LETTER BRAKE // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Stop Nonessential — S — stop every nonessential movement.
2. Take Physical — T — take one physical step back.
3. Observe Facts — O — observe facts, sensations, and the strongest impulse.
4. Proceed Safely — P — proceed with the smallest safe move that will still make sense in an hour.
5. Dont Negotiate — Do not negotiate with momentum between letters.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Dont Negotiate is your cue to stop.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ONE FOOT HERE, ONE FOOT NEAR IT // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Choose Stable — Choose a stable anchor such as feet on the floor or a fixed sound.
2. Keep Most — Keep most attention there while allowing a small edge of distress into awareness.
3. Anchor Verify — Verify the anchor remains present.
4. Adjust — Adjust the ratio until both can coexist without losing choice.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Adjust, you are done.

2. At Anchor Verify, name the sensation in plain physical words—pressure, heat, tightness, movement.
3. When you reach Adjust, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Hold distress and safety in the same frame.

Panic & body alarm

under 2 minutes

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
A large release can become several manageable ones.

GAME MOVE
Open at Let Air; close at Wait Body. Keep it light and literal.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EXHALE IN CHAPTERS // PLAY
One clean round. Keep the moves simple.

1. Let Air — Instead of one continuous out-breath, let air leave in three soft portions with tiny unforced spaces between.
2. Keep Face — Keep the face loose and never push to empty.
3. Wait Body — After the final segment, wait for the body’s next inhale rather than grabbing it.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Wait Body be enough.

3. When you reach Wait Body, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Carry this rule with you: A large release can become several manageable ones.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 EXPAND–GATHER–EXPAND // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Acknowledge — First, acknowledge the full weather of the moment.
2. Breathe Small — Next, gather attention around breathing as a small centre.
3. Widen Whole — Finally, widen to the whole body and surrounding space.
4. Spend — Spend roughly one minute in each shape.
5. Carry Final — Carry the final wide frame into your next movement.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Carry Final, you are done.

Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Walking can become a moving attention track.

GAME MOVE
Play from Place Weight to Finish Walking. Treat the last move as the finish line.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 FOUR PARTS OF ONE STEP // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Place Weight — Slow enough to distinguish lift, travel, place, and weight transfer.
2. Follow Events — Follow those four events through several steps.
3. Thought — When thought pulls away, rejoin at whichever phase the foot is currently performing.
4. Finish Walking — Finish by walking normally while retaining one point of contact.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Finish Walking and release the exercise.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Place Weight, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Thought, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Finish Walking, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Walking can become a moving attention track.

Enter through Choose Sensation; leave as soon as you reach Return Fact. One pass is enough.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 NOTICE THE NOTICING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact.

⚡ DONE — Complete Return Fact, then return to your day.

Enter through Choose Sensation; leave as soon as you reach Return Fact. One pass is enough.

🎮 NOTICE THE NOTICING // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose Sensation — Choose any sensation.
2. Recognise — First recognise its qualities.
3. Ask Verbally — Then ask, without answering verbally, ‘How is this already known?’ Rest with the immediacy of knowing rather than searching for an object called awareness.
4. Return Fact — Return by naming one visible fact.

⚡ DONE — Complete Return Fact, then return to your day.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. At the start of Choose Sensation, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Ask Verbally, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
The old reaction loses a little speed before Return Fact.

📸 MY RESULT
“I moved attention from what was loud to what was useful.”

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 BORROW THE SKY’S WIDTH // PLAY
Keep it literal. One round, then out.

1. Open Sky — Gaze softly into open sky or another unobstructed safe field.
2. Release Pinpoint — Release pinpoint focus and include the edges of vision.
3. Compare Width — Without forcing calm, compare the width outside with the contraction inside.
4. Allow Attention — Allow attention to occupy both.

⚡ EXIT MOVE — Allow Attention is your cue to stop.

GOAL

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THE BODY AS INNER SPACE // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Imagine Torso — Imagine the torso and limbs as volumes containing room rather than dense objects.
2. Cavities — Notice cavities, distances, and open intervals inside the body mental picture while maintaining feet, seat, and external sense of where you are.
3. Keep Image — Keep the image gentle and anatomically nonliteral.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Keep Image be enough.

items.unique_game_move: One round only: enter at Wait Pull, finish at Name Object.
items.recognition_cue: If the old reaction is running before you notice it, Catch Wanting Before The Object turns the mental noise into one playable move.

items.immediate_need: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Automatic habits & autopilot

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
If the old reaction is running before you notice it, Catch Wanting Before The Object turns the mental noise into one playable move.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Wait Pull, finish at Name Object.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 CATCH WANTING BEFORE THE OBJECT // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Wait Pull — Wait at the first pull: leaning, brightening, reaching, mental zoom.
2. Observe Wanting — For five seconds, observe wanting as raw movement without completing ‘I want…’.
3. Name Object — Only afterward name the object and decide whether pursuit serves the wider situation.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Name Object and release the exercise.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Wait Pull, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Observe Wanting, move your attention to one thing that is happening now.
3. When you reach Name Object, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Use this as the exit rule: Desire starts moving before it names a destination.

🎮 NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

items.mission: Release both hands of mental grasping.

items.how_to_play:
🎮 NOT FOR, NOT AGAINST // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Whether — Notice whether experience is being pulled closer or pushed away.
2. Relax — Relax the corresponding inner movement without demanding neutrality.
3. Let Content — Let the content remain unowned and unobstructed for a short interval.
4. Act According — Then act according to circumstance, not attraction or aversion.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Act According, you are done.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 REMOVE THE NAME BADGES // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Name — Name the roles active today.
2. Imagine Badge — One by one, imagine placing each badge on a table—parent, worker, partner, achiever, patient, helper.
3. Release Roles — Sit without using any badge to answer ‘Who am I now?’ After a short pause, reclaim only the role needed next.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Release Roles be enough.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE FEELINGS BACK IN ORDER // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Name Mix — Name up to three present feelings. Do not explain them yet.
2. Find First — Which arrived first? Put it at the left of a short line.
3. Link Cue — Add the concrete cue that each feeling answered—words heard, an image, a body change, or a later thought.
4. Read Order — Read the sequence once: ‘First ___ answered ___; then ___ answered ___.’ Stop after the order is clear.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Read Order and release the exercise.

🎮 THE THREE QUALITIES WEATHER REPORT // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Classify — Classify the current movement as clarity, agitation, inertia, or a mixture.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Count Gap be enough.

TRIGGER
Action avoidance & procrastination

PLAY TIME
about 90 seconds

HOOK
Do Not Replace The Last Thought gives you a quick reset for the moment when your mind keeps delaying the first move.

GOAL
Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Wait Thought; stop the moment you complete Count Gap.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DO NOT REPLACE THE LAST THOUGHT // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Wait Thought — Wait for a thought to end naturally.
2. Empty — At the first empty beat, resist generating commentary about emptiness.
3. Rest Duration — Rest for the duration available—even a fraction.
4. Let Thought — Let the next thought arise without invitation.
5. Count Gap — Count the gap only after it is over.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Count Gap be enough.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Wait Thought, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Rest Duration, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Count Gap, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Silence often disappears because the mind fills it immediately.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You can finish at Count Gap even if the original thought has not completely disappeared.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE MEMORY BACK IN PAST TENSE // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Use Happened — Retell one short segment using was, happened, had, and then.
2. After — After every emotionally loaded sentence, insert three present facts: where you are, what year it is, and what choice exists now.
3. Finish Moment — Finish with ‘That ended; this moment is different.’.

⚡ END MOVE — Finish Moment. No second lap.

GOAL

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THREE SELVES, THREE JOBS // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Make Columns — Make columns for PAST, PRESENT, FUTURE.
2. Complete Actions — Put completed actions under past, available repair under present, and prevention plans under future.
3. Cross Out — Cross out any item assigned to the wrong self.
4. Perform — Perform only one present-column task now.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Perform, you are done.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. When you arrive at Make Columns, press both feet down for three seconds.
2. At Cross Out, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Perform, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Present-you should not perform every time period’s labour.

📸 MY RESULT
“I stopped waiting to feel ready and found one move I could do.”

items.trigger_play_time:
TRIGGER
Urgency & decision pressure

PLAY TIME
under 2 minutes

HOOK
Put The Years Back Between Them catches the moment when the fastest response feels like the only response and gives you another route.
items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Put the real years back between then and now.

GAME MOVE
Start at Date Events. Stop at Recheck Urgency. Let the middle do the work.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 PUT THE YEARS BACK BETWEEN THEM // PLAY
One short round. Nothing to solve beyond the moves.

1. Date Events — Picture the dates of the events that currently feel piled together.
2. Scale Distance — Give equal physical space to equal spans of time; do not place every event in one crowded cluster.
3. Present — Notice TODAY at the correct distance and name one fact that belongs only to now.
4. Recheck Urgency — Look again at the oldest event and rate how immediate it feels after the spacing is restored.

⚡ FINISH — Recheck Urgency closes the round.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Before you begin Date Events, let your shoulders drop and take one easy exhale.
2. At Present, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Recheck Urgency, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Put the real years back between then and now.

items.potency_3: When you reach Recheck Urgency, choose one action that fits the facts you found. If you remember one thing, make it this: Put the real years back between then and now.
items.win_reward:
🏆 WIN SIGNAL
You arrive at Recheck Urgency with less need to obey the first answer.

📸 MY RESULT
“I created one beat between 'now' and 'do it.'”
items.formula_flow: Date Events → Scale Distance → Present → Recheck Urgency

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.

GAME MOVE
Give yourself one clean run: Rewrite Broken first, Add Condition last.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 DELETE ‘AM’ FROM THE SENTENCE // PLAY
Play the moves, not the whole life story.

1. Rewrite Broken — Rewrite ‘I am broken/lazy/anxious’ without am or is.
2. Use Temporary — Use temporary action language: ‘Avoiding has increased this week,’ ‘Anxiety is moving through the chest,’ ‘Energy dropped after…’.
3. Add Condition — Add one condition under which the process changes.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Add Condition, you are done.

2. At Use Temporary, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Add Condition, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep the clean version: Identity verbs can turn weather into a prison.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

GAME MOVE
Begin where it says Describe Event; stop the moment you complete Distance.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 THIRD-PERSON OWNERSHIP TEST // PLAY
Treat it like a mini experiment—one run, then stop.

1. Describe Event — Say the event once as ‘this mind is predicting…’ or ‘the system is producing…’.
2. Change — Notice what changes in intensity, responsibility, and choice.
3. Return Person — Then return to first person for the action you genuinely own: ‘I will…’.
4. Distance — Distance the content, not agency.

⚡ CLOSE — Let Distance be enough.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. Right before the first move, Describe Event, let one breath happen without trying to improve it.
2. At Return Person, ask, “What can I do in under two minutes?”.
3. When you reach Distance, choose one action that fits the facts you found. The useful rule here is simple: Grammar can loosen the grip without denying the experience.

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 ADD THE WITNESS WHO SHOULD HAVE BEEN THERE // PLAY
Keep this round small: just the listed moves.

1. Introduce — Introduce a compassionate observer appropriate to the event—a trusted adult, advocate, elder, clinician, or current-you.
2. Name Wrong — Have them name what was wrong, what protection was deserved, and what is true about the person who endured it.
3. Keep Words — Keep their words believable.

⚡ STOP POINT — Once you reach Keep Words, you are done.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 RELATIONSHIP DATA, NOT ONE BIG FEELING // PLAY
Play it once. No bonus analysis.

1. Hold In Your Mind Event — For recent interactions, Keep event, context, frequency, repair attempt, and outcome in separate columns.
2. Look Repetition — Look for repetition and exceptions.
3. Issue Narrow — Issue a narrow conclusion tied to the observed period rather than ‘always’ or ‘never.’.

⚡ END MOVE — Issue Narrow. No second lap.

items.goal_why_game_move:
GOAL
Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Return Define, finish at Evaluate.
items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Return Define — Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
2. Specify — Specify what evidence would show each over time.
3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Evaluate and release the exercise.
items.potency_stack:
⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Return Define, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Specify, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Evaluate, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

items.plain:
APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS

TRIGGER
Emotional reasoning

PLAY TIME
30–60 seconds

HOOK
Try Apology Needs Three Evidence Points when a strong feeling is starting to sound like a fact. It creates just enough space for a different response.

GOAL
Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

GAME MOVE
One round only: enter at Return Define, finish at Evaluate.

HOW TO PLAY
🎮 APOLOGY NEEDS THREE EVIDENCE POINTS // PLAY
Follow the sequence once; leave the rest alone.

1. Return Define — Define what adequate repair requires: clear acknowledgement, changed action, and prevention of return.
2. Specify — Specify what evidence would show each over time.
3. Evaluate — Check the apology against those criteria rather than immediate emotion.

⚡ LAST MOVE — Reach Evaluate and release the exercise.

⚡ POWER-UPS
1. To open Return Define, slow the next movement by about half.
2. At Specify, give the feeling a name without letting it make the decision.
3. When you reach Evaluate, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Your takeaway: Repair is a behaviour pattern, not a tone of voice.

🏆 WIN SIGNAL
By the time you reach Evaluate, the problem looks a little more workable.

📸 MY RESULT
“The feeling was real. It still wasn't the whole evidence.”

FORMULA FLOW
Return Define → Specify → Evaluate

items.play_the_loop:
HOW TO PLAY
🎮 SET THE CONTACT DOSE // PLAY
Run the game exactly once, lightly.

1. Choose Frequency — Before contact, choose frequency, duration, permitted topics, location, and exit phrase.
2. Start Lowest — Start with the lowest dose that preserves both connection and regulation.
3. Use Body — Review afterward using body and behaviour, not guilt.

⚡ DONE — Complete Use Body, then return to your day.

1. At the start of Choose Frequency, widen your gaze and notice the edges of the room.
2. At Start Lowest, look for the piece of evidence your first reaction ignored.
3. When you reach Use Body, choose one action that fits the facts you found. Keep only this lesson: Closeness can be realistic instead of accepted or abandoned completely.
